Z3-universality test patterns for VEX ops
------------------------------------------

When a new VEX op has a Z3 symbolic path (``#[cfg(feature = "vex-engine-z3")]``
tests in ``native/angr/src/vex/ops.rs`` and ``symbolic/value_tests.rs``),
step 6 ("Test") in the worked example above is not enough on its own --
use one of these three templates depending on what reference is available:

1. **Python-parity template.** When
   ``angr/engines/vex/claripy/irop.py`` defines an explicit reference
   (``_op_Iop_X``, e.g. ``_op_Iop_Reverse32sIn64_x2`` at line 599),
   reconstruct the same ``Concat`` pattern using ``RustBV`` extract +
   ``concat_le_elements``. Then: ``push()`` -> ``add_constraint(got._eq(&py).not())``
   -> ``assert(!is_sat())`` -> ``pop()``. Claripy's bit-index convention
   (``arg[127:96]`` = high 32 bits) maps directly to
   ``RustBV.extract(127, 96, &ctx)``; ``concat_le_elements`` indexes 0 as
   LSB, so slices are pushed LSB->MSB. Confirmed for ``VReverse``
   (``Iop_Reverse32sIn64_x2``) and ``VQAdd`` (``Iop_QAdd8Sx8``); see
   ``test_vec_reverse_32in64_x2_symbolic_matches_python_ref``.

2. **Spec-replay template.** For VEX ops with no claripy reference (no
   ``_op_generic_X``), build a "spec-replay" reference using the same
   ``RustBV`` primitives as the helper under test but inlined in the
   test itself. This catches structural encoding errors (wrong cap,
   swapped then/else, off-by-one extract, sign-bit confusion) as a SAT
   counter-example, but is weaker than full parity -- a bug in the spec
   itself is not caught. Examples:
   ``test_vqshl_16x4_symbolic_universal_unsigned``,
   ``test_vqsal_16x4_symbolic_universal_signed``.

3. **Roundtrip template.** For IR rewrite rules in ``symbolic::value``,
   pin every symbolic value with concrete values via a constraint, then
   call ``ctx.eval()`` -- purely structural assertions about the
   ``RustBV`` tree miss semantic bugs (e.g. wrong byte order). Use a
   ``raw_extract_node`` helper that bypasses ``extract_into`` to verify
   the Z3-emission hook independently of the construction-time hook.
   This is the right pattern for any rewrite with dual hook points
   (construction-time and Z3-emit). Examples: ``test_pre_z3_extract_*``,
   ``test_extract_over_reverse_*`` in ``value_tests.rs``.

When evaluating a new VEX op: check ``irop.py`` for ``_op_Iop_*`` or
``_op_generic_*`` first -- if present, use template 1; otherwise use
template 2 (with its caveat); for a rewrite with both a construction-time
and a Z3-emit hook, use template 3.

reason: Generalizable Rust test-writing gotcha for the with_z3_context helper: the closure is Send+Sync-bound to prevent smuggling !Send Z3 pointers across context boundaries, so tests must cast pointers to usize before/inside the closure rather than passing raw Z3 pointers in or out. Not duplicated in docs; useful whenever writing a new multi-context test.
